title: OUR GOD IS A CONSUMING FIRE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: For the Lord your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God. After you have had children and grandchildren and have lived in the land a long time—if you then become corrupt and make any kind of idol, doing evil in the eyes of the Lord your God and arousing his anger, I call the heavens and the earth as witnesses against you this day that you will quickly perish from the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess. You will not live there long but will certainly be destroyed. - Deut 4:24-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses uses striking language: "The Lord your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God." These are weighty words we should not soften. God's "jealousy" is not the petty envy of a small heart, but the righteous, passionate love of a God who will not share His people's devotion with false gods. Just as a faithful spouse rightly refuses to share their marriage with a rival, God rightly claims the exclusive worship of His people. His jealousy flows from His holy love.

And He is "a consuming fire" — utterly holy, unwilling to leave sin and idolatry untouched. This is a sobering picture. God takes covenant faithfulness seriously, and He warned that persistent idolatry would bring devastating consequences. We should let these words fill us with reverent awe. God is not to be trifled with; He is holy, and His holiness is like a fire.

We might be tempted to shy away from this image, preferring to think only of God's gentleness. But Scripture holds together God's love and His holiness. The New Testament repeats this very phrase: "our God is a consuming fire" (Heb 12:29). The God we worship is holy, and His holiness calls us to reverent, wholehearted devotion.

Yet here is the wonder of the gospel: the consuming fire of God's holiness, which our sin deserves, fell upon Christ in our place. Jesus bore the judgment of God so that we could draw near to the holy God without being consumed. Now we can approach Him with reverence and awe, yet also with confidence, because Christ has made us acceptable (Heb 12:28). Let us worship God with holy reverence, giving Him the exclusive devotion His jealous, holy love deserves.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you hold together God's love and His holiness in your view of Him?
2. What does it mean that God's "jealousy" is His passionate, holy love for you?
3. How does Christ enable you to approach the consuming fire with confidence?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy God, You are a consuming fire, jealous for the devotion of Your people. Fill me with reverent awe, and thank You that Christ bore Your judgment so I can draw near. Help me worship You with wholehearted, exclusive devotion. Amen.
